Definition: properly, the palate or inside of the mouth; hence, the mouth itself (as the organ of speech, taste and kissing)
BiblicalUsage: The palate is the mouth that tastes, and the word is used for tasting words and for the tongue that will not move. The ear tries words as the mouth tastes meat, Ezekiel's tongue cleaves to the roof of his mouth so he cannot reprove, and Hosea is told to set the trumpet to his mouth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mouth is the place where truth is tasted and spoken: Job tastes words the way the mouth tastes meat. Ezekiel's silence is itself a judgement on a rebellious house, and Hosea's trumpet shows the mouth is also where warning is sounded.
